grader.scenario: Broadband connection dropping specifically during microwave usage; resolved via 5 GHz SSID split but unverified on call
grader.notes: Okay call featuring failed branding, dead air breaches, rude remarks, unverified resolution due to dinner time testing, and handled empathy in the middle third.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent failed standard opening branding ('Broadband faults desk...') and closing branding.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Agent allowed two separate unmanaged dead air gaps of 40 seconds at turns 14 and 34.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Verified full postal address and security PIN within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer as Rory throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: At [05:31] the customer angrily rejected the claim that her new microwave was a hazard; the agent kept lecturing about magnetrons and never acknowledged her frustration.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent accurately paraphrased microwave interference issue at turn 2.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Agent completed harmless recheck of customer address at turn 41.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Agent split SSIDs, shifted 2.4 GHz channel to 1, guided 5 GHz connection, and waived router fee.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Agent insulted customer at turn 11: 'If you operate a faulty, unshielded microwave oven with deteriorated door seals that leaks radiation into living areas, that is a domestic appliance hazard, not an S-Net telecommunications fault.'

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent asked about router proximity and kitchen layout.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Customer was unable to run microwave test until dinner, leaving issue unverified on call.
